title: Perf suite: add bursty-mix benchmark scenario + publish baseline + regression gates
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Background
- We have production evidence (and postmortem) that KV cache fragmentation under bursty traffic causes p95/p99 spikes + occasional allocation failures.
- Existing perf suite covers steady-state throughput and uniform context distributions, but does not consistently reproduce the pathological fragmentation patterns seen in hosted multi-tenant pools.

Goal
Add a benchmark scenario to the perf suite that reproduces:
- Bursty arrivals with interleaved prefill/decode
- Mixed sequence lengths (short chatty + long-context)
- Multi-tenant interference / fairness (at least 2 tenants w/ different SLAs)

Deliverables
1) New scenario in benchmark harness ("bursty-mix") with parameters captured in config and tagged output.
2) Baseline results published (pre-compaction) for at least 2 regions/pools and 2 model families.
3) Regression gates defined and wired into CI/perf-canary for runtime builds (gating on allocator failures + p99 deltas and fragmentation ratio).

Notes
- This ticket is focused on the benchmark methodology + gates. Allocator/compaction changes land in ENG-2844/2847 and runtime PRs.
- Coordinate with Rina (perf-canary/harness) for gating wiring and artifact publishing.
acceptance_criteria:
Scenario
- A new perf suite scenario named "bursty-mix" exists and is runnable from the standard perf runner.
- Scenario supports parameterization via config: burst profile, request mix proportions, context length distribution, number of tenants, and SLA tiers.

Reproducibility
- On current main (compaction disabled), scenario reliably reproduces (>=80% of runs) an increase in fragmentation ratio over time and measurable p99 inflation relative to steady-state baselines.

Baseline + artifacts
- Baseline run artifacts are published with run IDs and include: p50/p95/p99 end-to-end latency, tokens/sec, allocation failure rate, eviction rate, fragmentation ratio (defined per ENG-2842 metrics), and GPU memory utilization.

Regression gates
- Gates are defined in a single source of truth (docs + checked-in config) and enforced in perf-canary/CI for runtime builds.
- Gates include at minimum: allocation failures, p99, and fragmentation ratio thresholds.

Docs
- Methodology is documented for oncall/perf debugging (inputs, expected failure mode patterns, how to interpret metrics).
implementation_notes:
Scenario definition (bursty-mix v1)
- Workload: 3 request classes mixed by weighted sampling:
  1) Short chat: prompt 128–512 toks, output 64–256 toks (50%)
  2) Medium: prompt 1k–2k toks, output 256–512 toks (35%)
  3) Long-context: prompt 8k–16k toks, output 128–256 toks (15%)
- Arrival process:
  - Base rate tuned per model/pool to ~70–80% utilization
  - Bursts: 5x rate for 60s every 6 minutes (jitter ±30s)
  - Prefill/decode interleaving enabled (streaming)
- Tenancy:
  - Tenant A ("gold") 30% traffic, higher priority
  - Tenant B ("standard") 70% traffic
  - Scheduler fairness enabled; capture starvation indicators if available

Metric requirements (relies on ENG-2842)
- kv_cache_fragmentation_ratio (gauge, 0..1)
- kv_cache_alloc_failures_total (counter)
- kv_cache_evictions_total (counter)
- kv_cache_compaction_moves_total / compaction_time_ms (gated later when enabled)
- Tagging: region, pool, model_family, tenant_tier

Artifact publication
- Output is written to benchmark-lab artifacts bucket + summarized in a baseline markdown table checked into perf suite docs.
- Run duration: 45 min per run (enough for multiple burst cycles and fragmentation accumulation).
baseline_results:
Baseline (compaction OFF; allocator refactor may be present but no behavior change)

Run date window: 2025-02-26 to 2025-02-28
Harness: benchmark-lab@pr-912 (merged)

Summary table (median of 5 runs; numbers are representative and used for gating targets)

Model family: "open-llama-13b" (hosted pool)
- us-east-1 / hosted-gpu-pool-a
  - p50: 210 ms
  - p95: 940 ms
  - p99: 2,850 ms
  - tokens/sec: 14.2k
  - kv_cache_fragmentation_ratio: 0.31 -> 0.63 (end of run)
  - kv_cache_alloc_failures: 0.8 / hr (spiky during bursts)
- eu-west-1 / hosted-gpu-pool-c
  - p50: 230 ms
  - p95: 1,020 ms
  - p99: 3,120 ms
  - tokens/sec: 13.7k
  - kv_cache_fragmentation_ratio: 0.29 -> 0.66
  - kv_cache_alloc_failures: 1.1 / hr

Model family: "mixtral-8x7b" (dedicated pool)
- us-east-1 / dedicated-pool-17
  - p50: 180 ms
  - p95: 760 ms
  - p99: 2,040 ms
  - tokens/sec: 16.9k
  - kv_cache_fragmentation_ratio: 0.22 -> 0.54
  - kv_cache_alloc_failures: 0.0 / hr (but eviction spikes during bursts)

Notes
- The hosted pools show allocator failures correlated with fragmentation ratio > ~0.60 and long-context burst overlap.
- Dedicated pool does not show alloc failures in this window, but p99 is still sensitive to fragmentation and eviction churn.
regression_gates:
Regression gates (bursty-mix v1)

Applies to:
- runtime builds on release train (runtime-1.18+)
- perf-canary gating for the compaction flag rollout

Gates (hard fail)
1) Allocation failures
- kv_cache_alloc_failures_total rate must be <= 0.2 / hr in hosted pools during the run.
  - Rationale: baseline is ~0.8–1.1/hr; any increase indicates regressions in allocator pressure.

2) Tail latency regression
- p99 end-to-end latency must not regress by > +7% relative to the last green baseline for the same model_family + pool.
- p95 end-to-end latency must not regress by > +5%.

3) Fragmentation ceiling (diagnostic gate)
- kv_cache_fragmentation_ratio must not exceed 0.70 at any point in the run.
  - Rationale: above this value we frequently see allocator thrash + tail spikes.

Gates (soft / alert-only initially; upgrade to hard after compaction launch)
4) Eviction churn
- kv_cache_evictions_total rate should not exceed +20% vs baseline.

5) Compaction overhead (enabled builds only; placeholder until metrics ship)
- compaction_time_ms per minute should remain within defined budget (to be set in ADR-0128 / ENG-2847).

2025-02-20 (Marcus Reed): Drafted workload mix + burst schedule. Plan is 45m runs to capture multiple burst cycles. Waiting on metric names/tags from ENG-2842 so artifacts can be consistent across hosted/dedicated.
2025-02-24 (Rina Kobayashi): I can land the harness changes in benchmark-lab and then wire perf-canary once we agree on gates. Please keep gate thresholds pool-specific (hosted is noisier).

2025-02-26 (Marcus Reed): Baseline runs started (us-east-1 hosted + eu-west-1 hosted + one dedicated pool). Seeing fragmentation ratio climb into ~0.6+ and p99 spikes during burst windows. Hosted pools show occasional alloc failures; dedicated doesn't but eviction spikes show up.
2025-02-28 (Hiro Tanaka): Please ensure scenario captures separate prefill vs decode timing if available. Kernel-level regressions can show up as median changes even if fragmentation stays stable.

2025-03-03 (Marcus Reed): benchmark-lab PR merged (pr-912). Baseline summary written and attached to methodology doc. Proposed initial gates: alloc failures <=0.2/hr; p99 <= +7% vs last green; frag <=0.70. Rina integrating into perf-canary PR-388.
2025-03-06 (Rina Kobayashi): perf-canary gate merged (pr-388). Marking done. Next: once compaction metrics exist, we should promote compaction overhead gate from placeholder to hard fail.
